The destination would be chosen only to cause the flight plan route to cross Cuba. The passengers could be a group of college students off on a holiday or any grouping of persons with a common interest to support chartering a non-scheduled flight."

Lemnitzer and the Joint Chiefs worked out a complex deception:

An aircraft at Elgin AFB would be painted and numbered as an exact duplicate for a civil registered aircraft belonging to a CJA proprietary organization in the Miami area. At a designated time the duplicate would be substituted for the actual civil aircraft and would be loaded with the selected passengers, all boarded under carefully prepared aliases. The actual registered aircraft would be converted to a drone [a remotely controlled unmanned aircraft]. Take off times of the drone aircraft and the actual aircraft will be scheduled to allow a rendezvous south of Florida.

From the rendezvous point the passenger-carrying aircraft will descend to minimum altitude and go directly into an auxiliary field at Elgin AFB where arrangements will have been made to evacuate the passengers and return the aircraft to its original status. The drone aircraft meanwhile will continue to fly the filed flight plan. When over Cuba the drone will be transmitting on the international distress frequency a "May Day" message stating he is under attack by Cuban MiG aircraft. The transmission will be interrupted by destruction of the aircraft, which will be triggered by radio signal. This will allow ICAO [International Civil Aviation Organization radio stations in the Western Hemisphere to tell the U.S. what has happened to the aircraft instead of the U.S. trying to "sell" the incident. http://whatreallyhappened.com/WRHARTICLES/northwoods.html

TIL Some biofuels are worse than crude oil.

I see biofuels is a dead end. Basically we're cutting down forests in poor countries to grow biofuels for our cars and trucks. There are plenty of issues with biofuels.

Instead of addressing the problem of our exponential technological growth on a finite planet, we just try to replace one problem (oil) with another (biofuels). It's going to get really obvious when the Chinese and the Indians will all want to drive SUVs, eat meat everyday and own tons of electronic gadgets just like we do.

Well, I'm pretty optimistic that we'll figure it out one way or another, maybe in a slow and disorderly manner, but we'll adapt.

Teslas outsell Mitsubichi, Suzuki, Olsmobile, Lincoln, Cadillac, Fiat, Land Rover, Porche, Buick and Volvo in California. I'm seeing solar arrays on more and more roofs every day. My computer used to be a big loud, power hog, now it only needs to be plugged in minutes a day. There are more options to by locally produced food and beer. There are major innovations every day like solar glass, vertical hydroponic farming and the powerwall.

Even biofuels are getting better. Palm and rapeseed oil were really just a primitive version. Now they're using agricultural waste and getting more bang for the buck without cutting into food production. Next it'll probably come from waste management and sewage treatment will pay for itself and landfills will be gold mines.
But that is not the only reason to use biofuels. Another is renewable energy and energy independance.

Well, climate change is environmental priority #1. Energy independence and renewables for the sake of renewables can wait. We are already capable of both btw. But I'm not sure we can reduce our carbon footprint fast enough to adapt to climate change.
